lots.guide_summary: Everything is SOLD Gowans hammer, AUD, no conversion, premium extra. Single plain myrtle slabs listed Jun to Sep 2026 sold for $10 to $60, with one $110. Prices have fallen: the last six sales (Sep 2026) were $13 to $20, and the Aug batch of long slabs was $25 to $55. No UNSOLD or ASKING evidence. Another 6 SLAB OF MYRTLE lots (445935 to 445940) are in this sale, so supply is plentiful.
lots.working: Keep: the lowest same-item SOLD hammer in the last 3 months is $10 (lot 428211, a long plain myrtle slab, photo viewed). $10 / 1.198 = $8.35, rounded down to $5. A realistic all-in for this slab is about $15 to $40 (hammer $13 to $35). Flip: likely resale is about $25 (the recent median of comparable sales), with $0 fees on a free local Gumtree or Marketplace listing and $0 postage (pickup only). $25 / 2.396 = $10.43, rounded down to $10. Not a worthwhile flip.
lots.confidence_reason: Chalk lot 1109 and date 23/10/26 read in the photo, and the Gowans title says myrtle. There are many opened same-venue SOLD results, and I checked photos of several. The species is not confirmed beyond the title, and the size and thickness are unknown.
lots.dropped_entries: Dropped the researcher's UNSOLD 'none found' placeholder (not evidence). Dropped lot 402725 '2 SLABS OF MYRTLE' $180 (two slabs, not the same item), 397899 'FIGURED MYRTLE' $110 and 388124 'TIGER MYRTLE' $60 (figured stock, unlike this plain slab). Kept 387981 $125 as an old high-water mark only. All researcher prices I checked against the API matched exactly.
lots.key_photo_findings: Chalk '1109 23/10/26' with a lot sticker. One narrow slab, roughly 2.3 to 2.5 m long and perhaps 25 to 35 cm wide at most. Orange-red heartwood consistent with myrtle, plain grain with no visible tiger or fiddleback figure. About a third of the width on the right edge is grey, weathered, punky-looking sapwood and bark with a waney edge. There is a knot about halfway up and checking at the top end. Not dressed.
lots.condition: Raw, rough-sawn and weathered. The sapwood edge and end checks will be lost when it is cut, so the usable clear heartwood is narrow, maybe 15 to 20 cm. Thickness unknown.
lots.question_for_gowans: What are the length, width and thickness of lot 1109, and how sound is the grey sapwood edge (rot or just weathering)? Is it air-dried?

lots.dropped_entries: Dropped the researcher's '$220 / $180' entry as mislabelled: $220 (387811) was 3 SLABS, so it is not the same item. The $180 two-slab result is kept inside the aggregate as the 12-month top. Single-slab figures were cited but I did not re-check them, so they are not used. lots.key_photo_findings: Chalk '1110 23/10/26' on both slabs, with a lot sticker. Left slab: wider (perhaps 30 to 35 cm), with a bark and waney edge at mid-height, several small knots and a pale cream colour. Right slab: narrow (about 20 to 25 cm), with a long dark crack running most of its length and a small hole. Both are paler and creamier than the golden 1119 pair. The colour fits Huon sapwood or young growth, but could also suggest another pale species. No figure.
lots.condition: Rough-sawn, unseasoned look. The right slab's full-length crack greatly reduces its usable width. Below average for the series, closer to the $35 lot 444302 than to the $105 pairs.
lots.question_for_gowans: Lot 1110: please confirm the species is Huon pine (it is paler than usual), give each slab's length, width and thickness, and say whether the crack in the narrow slab goes right through.
